investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-06T16:01–16:08Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state, so the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create was violated in full.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for peer-pod VMs at the time of the eval run. Because the pod never scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885) never returned a VM identity, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the contract validation to fail completely. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was unscheduled for 147s before the check timed out.

failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was written, consistent with the pod never starting.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are listed as missing, matching the empty evidence object.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error message, latencyMs=149144, evidenceKeys=[] — confirms the same capacity constraint blocked a second independent pod.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error message, latencyMs=152940, evidenceKeys=[] — confirms a third independent pod was also blocked.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: all existing VM slots are occupied by live or leaked remote agent pods, leaving zero allocatable capacity for new probe pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message across all three sibling checks (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec targets a specific node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the effective scheduling pool to those 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are also at VM capacity, no fallback exists. Supported by '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' in failed-check.message.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods from prior eval runs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them: the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs is intended to release resources, but if a prior run crashed before cleanup, slots may remain occupied.

Quaternary — cluster under-provisioned for concurrent eval load: all three sibling checks ran within the same ~7-minute window (16:01–16:08Z), each requesting a VM slot simultaneously, potentially exhausting a small pool that would otherwise recover between sequential runs.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes have Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) could not schedule a peer-pod VM, the probe never reached the state-polling stage and returned zero evidence, violating the required-evidence contract for orgId, agentId, readyState, and state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across the two eligible nodes. With no schedulable capacity and no preemption victims available, every attempt to create a remote agent pod fails at the scheduler before any application logic runs. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion on the production Kubernetes cluster, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct and accurate reflection of this infrastructure condition. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-eligible nodes: all allocatable peer-pod VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: those nodes are not labeled or tainted to accept remote-agent pods, so even if vm capacity existed elsewhere in the cluster it would not be usable without affinity changes.

Tertiary — no preemption policy configured or no lower-priority pods present on the two eligible nodes: the scheduler explicitly reports 'No preemption victims found', meaning the cluster cannot self-heal by evicting lower-priority workloads.

Out-of-scope hypothesis — eval runner misconfiguration: the runner correctly reached the createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) and the error originates from the Kubernetes API, not from a runner bug. This cause is considered low probability given the explicit scheduler message.

The pod remained unscheduled for ~145–147 seconds before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence output and failing every required-evidence assertion in the remote-agent-runtime contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent eval environment has exhausted its schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. Of the 6 available nodes, only 2 are eligible for kata peer-pod workloads and both reported insufficient VM capacity at scheduling time; the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1918) never executed, no agent was created, and the eval returned empty evidence — causing all five required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) to be missing and the message assertion ("hello from aura") to go unevaluated. This is an eval-infrastructure / cluster-capacity failure localized to the remote-agents feature in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-06T16:01–16:08Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state, so the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create was violated in full.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for peer-pod VMs at the time of the eval run. Because the pod never scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885) never returned a VM identity, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the contract validation to fail completely. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was unscheduled for 147s before the check timed out.
failed-check.timing: status=fail, latencyMs=153559, confirming the check ran to near-timeout without ever collecting evidence.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was written, consistent with the pod never starting.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are listed as missing, matching the empty evidence object.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error message, latencyMs=149144, evidenceKeys=[] — confirms the same capacity constraint blocked a second independent pod.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error message, latencyMs=152940, evidenceKeys=[] — confirms a third independent pod was also blocked.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: all existing VM slots are occupied by live or leaked remote agent pods, leaving zero allocatable capacity for new probe pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message across all three sibling checks (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec targets a specific node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the effective scheduling pool to those 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are also at VM capacity, no fallback exists. Supported by '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' in failed-check.message.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods from prior eval runs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them: the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs is intended to release resources, but if a prior run crashed before cleanup, slots may remain occupied.

Quaternary — cluster under-provisioned for concurrent eval load: all three sibling checks ran within the same ~7-minute window (16:01–16:08Z), each requesting a VM slot simultaneously, potentially exhausting a small pool that would otherwise recover between sequential runs.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes have Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) could not schedule a peer-pod VM, the probe never reached the state-polling stage and returned zero evidence, violating the required-evidence contract for orgId, agentId, readyState, and state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across the two eligible nodes. With no schedulable capacity and no preemption victims available, every attempt to create a remote agent pod fails at the scheduler before any application logic runs. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion on the production Kubernetes cluster, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct and accurate reflection of this infrastructure condition. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-eligible nodes: all allocatable peer-pod VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: those nodes are not labeled or tainted to accept remote-agent pods, so even if vm capacity existed elsewhere in the cluster it would not be usable without affinity changes.

Tertiary — no preemption policy configured or no lower-priority pods present on the two eligible nodes: the scheduler explicitly reports 'No preemption victims found', meaning the cluster cannot self-heal by evicting lower-priority workloads.

Out-of-scope hypothesis — eval runner misconfiguration: the runner correctly reached the createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) and the error originates from the Kubernetes API, not from a runner bug. This cause is considered low probability given the explicit scheduler message.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-06T16:06–16:08Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The pod remained unscheduled for ~145–147 seconds before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence output and failing every required-evidence assertion in the remote-agent-runtime contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent eval environment has exhausted its schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. Of the 6 available nodes, only 2 are eligible for kata peer-pod workloads and both reported insufficient VM capacity at scheduling time; the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1918) never executed, no agent was created, and the eval returned empty evidence — causing all five required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) to be missing and the message assertion ("hello from aura") to go unevaluated. This is an eval-infrastructure / cluster-capacity failure localized to the remote-agents feature in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes — concurrent eval runs, other workloads, or leaked/stuck peer-pod VMs from prior runs have consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for new scheduling.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes — the remote-agent pod requires a specific node label or taint (e.g. kata peer-pods capable nodes) that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the effective scheduling pool to those 2 already-exhausted nodes.

[Possible] Leaked or zombie peer-pod VMs from a previous eval run that did not clean up properly — the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs is present but a prior failure may have left VMs allocated, reducing available capacity.
[Possible] Cluster under-provisioning — only 2 kata-capable nodes exist in the production-api cluster, which may be insufficient to handle concurrent or back-to-back eval runs.

[Lower likelihood] A transient Kubernetes API or node-level issue caused the scheduler to report insufficient capacity even if slots were nominally available — would require scheduler logs to confirm or rule out.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the 2 eligible nodes shows unused slots at the time of the failure, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduler or admission-controller bug would need to be investigated.
If the pod's node affinity/selector is misconfigured and actually matches zero nodes (not 2), the root cause would shift from capacity exhaustion to a configuration error in the pod spec.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds without any manual intervention (e.g. VM slots freed on their own), it would suggest a transient capacity spike rather than a persistent exhaustion or leak.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed in the same run window, the cause would be localized to the runtime check's pod spec rather than shared cluster capacity.

If the Kubernetes scheduler logs show a different error (e.g. image pull failure, resource quota, or admission webhook rejection) rather than kata.peerpods.io/vm insufficiency, the diagnosis would need to be revised.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across all cluster nodes before attempting remote-agent provisioning, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct check status rather than a scheduling timeout.
Add a zombie/leaked-VM detection eval that lists pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources older than a configurable threshold and alerts if any are found outside of active eval windows.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies at least N nodes satisfy the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector and that each has at least 1 free kata.peerpods.io/vm slot, catching under-provisioning before it causes eval failures.

Consider adding a latency-bucketed retry eval for remote-agent-create that distinguishes 'pod never scheduled' (scheduler error) from 'pod scheduled but agent failed to start' (runtime error), enabling faster triage.
